one_liner: 2016 fork of ARM's 2015 astcenc 1.x CLI that reuses scratch buffers per thread; 1.2x-2.2x faster on one image, superseded.
what_it_does: A command-line ASTC texture compressor and decompressor (astcenc) forked from ARM-software/astc-encoder as of October 2015, meant as a binary swap-in for the astcenc inside the Mali GPU Texture Compression Tool. The CLI is the 1.x one: -c/-d/-t, block footprint and one preset (-veryfast to -exhaustive). It adds a -batchsize option (default 128 blocks) and drops -diag. There is no library API: the codec is the same set of Source/*.cpp files built into one executable.
how_it_is_fast: There are no algorithmic or SIMD changes; the gains come from housekeeping in ARM's reference encoder. Commit b5a2d16 removed the new/delete of large scratch structures that compress_symbolic_block_fixed_partition_1_plane/2_planes did on every call, for every partition candidate of every block. Each thread now allocates these buffers once. Commit 4766689 wraps them in a SymbolicBatchCompressor, and each thread encodes runs of 128 consecutive blocks instead of ARM's one-block round-robin; compress_symbolic_batch is just a loop over compress_symbolic_block. Commit 991edf8 compiles out the DEBUG_PRINT_DIAGNOSTICS code that upstream enabled by default, removing runtime print_diagnostics branches from the hot path.
when_to_use: Reproducing or patching a 2015-2016 Mali TCT / astcenc 1.x pipeline whose command line and output format you must keep, where a 1.2x-2x faster drop-in binary is the only change allowed.
Studying how much of the old ARM reference encoder's time went to heap churn: the diff is small, and readable as a case study.
when_not_to_use: Any new ASTC work. ARM's own astcenc 2.0 (August 2020) changelog charts show astcenc-avx2 2.0 at roughly 2x-3x the speed of astcenc 1.7 at -thorough and roughly 1.3x-4x at -fast/-medium, with PSNR mostly within about 0.2 dB. That was measured on a Core i5-9600K with 6 threads (chart readings approximate), and the 3.x-5.x releases are faster still. ARM's current encoder is also a library, has SIMD paths and is Apache-2.0.

Bit-exact reproduction of the original astcenc. Commit 00f9f3d moves 'separate_errors[best_partition] = 1e30f' ahead of the partition_sequence remapping in find_best_partitionings. That changes which dual-plane partition candidates are tried, so output can differ from the binary it claims to replace, and no PSNR comparison is published.

Commercial or redistributed tooling without legal review. The code is under ARM's Mali ASTC EULA v1.3: use only for the 'Authorised Purpose' of ASTC compression and decompression tools, no hardware development, non-transferable, and the licence must be shipped with any distribution.

Small textures on many cores. Work is handed out in 128-block batches per thread, so an image with fewer than threads x 128 blocks leaves threads idle unless you lower -batchsize (derived from encode_astc_image_threadfunc).

integration.form: command-line executable (prebuilt Win32/Win64 astcenc.exe in Binary/, or build Source/ with the Makefile or the VS2013 project); no library target
integration.dependencies: none beyond pthreads on POSIX (stb_image is vendored)
integration.min_toolchain: Makefile uses g++ -O3 -msse2 -mfpmath=sse with no -std flag. The README says GCC >= 4.6, but the batch code uses astc_decode_mode::DECODE_LDR (scoped access to an unscoped enum), which needs C++11, so use a compiler that defaults to C++11 or later or add -std=c++11. Visual Studio 2013 project for Windows.
integration.platforms: x86/x86-64 (Makefile forces -msse2 -mfpmath=sse); Windows binaries checked in; Linux/macOS from source
integration.thread_safety: multi-threaded internally (-j, defaults to the logical CPU count); each thread owns its SymbolicBatchCompressor scratch buffers; there is no API to call concurrently
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same 1.x command line and .astc output format as the Mali TCT/ARM 1.x astcenc, but -diag is removed, -batchsize is new, and dual-plane encodings can differ because of the partition-search fix

gotchas: The speed numbers are not at matched quality. The README claims 'some quality improvement' but reports no PSNR, even though the tool's own -t -showpsnr mode would have produced it.
-diag is gone. It prints '-diag switch is unsupported in this version', and defining DEBUG_PRINT_DIAGNOSTICS now trips a static_assert because diagnostics are 'broken in batch mode'.

The 'official astcenc (64-bit)' column is the October 2015 upstream code, not ARM's last 1.x release (1.7) and not 2.x or later. Its build (ARM's checked-in Win64 binary or the author's own) and compiler are not stated.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other ASTC encoder is catalogued yet. The texture-codec siblings (bc7e, bc7enc, etcpak, Goofy, ICBC, Basis Universal) target BC1/BC7/ETC, not ASTC. For ASTC, current ARM astcenc 4.x/5.x beats this fork on speed, quality evidence, licence and API, so pick this fork only when you must stay on the 1.x CLI.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party table: wall-clock seconds to compress turret_diffuse_map.png on an Intel Core i5 760, at each 1.x preset. Against the official 64-bit astcenc of the time the fork is 2.05x (veryfast), 2.15x (fast), 1.36x (medium), 1.30x (thorough) and 1.23x (exhaustive) faster; against the 32-bit Mali TCT binary it is 1.91x-2.60x (derived from page data). Block size, thread count (the i5 760 has 4 cores, and the default is autodetect), compiler, flags and output PSNR are not given.
status_note: Abandoned since 2016-06-12 (18 commits, 8 by the fork author; 1 star; one downstream fork, abusenius, with no extra commits; no PRs). Reference only: ARM's custom EULA, not Apache-2.0, and the code is the pre-2.0 reference encoder.
measurement_notes: Of the fork author's eight commits, five touch code (by their messages, 99fcb07 adds a header to the Makefile and 833427c fixes indentation; a0d8c7b updates the README and binaries). Reading them confirms that only 00f9f3d touches encoder decisions. In the dual-plane partition loop, it now marks the chosen candidate's error as 1e30 before the index is remapped through partition_sequence, so the loop no longer re-selects the same candidate. 44f4c63 and 4766689 only add the batch header, the SymbolicBatchCompressor wrapper and the per-thread batch loop, with no changed constants, cutoffs, iteration counts or presets. b5a2d16 replaces per-call new/delete with per-thread buffers, and 991edf8 removes 167 lines of diagnostic printing. So the timing table compares code that differs in output on dual-plane blocks, at unreported quality, against a baseline whose build is unidentified; this supports keeping tier C with the existing caveats. No correctness bug was found in the batching code (block ranges, the end-of-image batch clamp and the round-robin counter all check out). The one image used is not in the repository, and the ARM 2.0 changelog charts (i5-9600K, 6 threads) show that ARM's own rewrite exceeded these gains at near-equal PSNR. Leads (uncatalogued): ARM-software/astc-encoder 2.x-5.x as an entry against 1.7, with its own changelog performance charts; daoo/astcrt, a real-time ASTC encoder from a thesis, with no numbers in its README; etnlGD/UnityAstcGpuEncoder, a GPU pixel-shader ASTC encoder, not opened.
sources_read: WebSearch: ASTC texture encoder faster than astcenc benchmark github (snippets: Phoronix on astcenc 4.0 being 1.2x-1.6x faster than 3.7; astcrt; UnityAstcGpuEncoder)
